replies.text:
Checks (step 2):

- Automated abuse (brute force / flooding / mass sign-up / scraping): design mentions "including login requests" but describes no sign-in endpoint behaviour, rate limits or email/SMS; nothing stated to attack. Volume abuse of the log store is already listed (agreed threat 5). Not a gap.
- Staff/admin screens showing user-supplied content: staff read the "central log system", and the content shown there is caller-supplied — "the API gateway logs full request and response bodies". Script/formula content rendering in a privileged log console is not covered by the agreed list. Not covered.
- Deleting/moderating/refunding/role changes with no record: design states no such action. Not present.
- Personal/financial documents cacheable by browsers, proxies or CDNs: design states no page or download delivered to a browser. Not present.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, exports, emails, headers or another interpreting system: yes — "logs full request and response bodies ... to the central log system". Agreed list covers only disclosure, token theft and volume, not injection/forgery of log records. Not covered.
- Unconfirmed reviewer items: #1 and #2 are the same insider-read-of-logs weakness as agreed threats 1–4 (same harm, reworded); #3 duplicates agreed threat 1; #4 is real and uncovered → reported.

```json
{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-07",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["API gateway", "central log system", "log search console"],
    "dataStores": ["central log system (1 year retention)"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["caller to API gateway", "gateway to central log system", "log console to staff readers"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii", "credentials", "payment"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Caller-supplied bodies written into logs let an attacker forge log records and poison investigations",
      "scenario": "Any caller of the gateway controls the request body verbatim. Because full bodies are written into the central log system, a caller can embed newlines and well-formed fake log records, or spoofed timestamps, user ids and error lines, inside a normal request. The log pipeline stores them as if the gateway emitted them. The attacker then hides their own real calls among forged entries, blames another account, or breaks parsing of the affected log stream, so responders investigating an integration or payment incident work from records the attacker wrote.",
      "component": "API gateway body logging into central log system",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "the API gateway logs full request and response bodies, including login requests and payment details, to the central log system for 1 year" }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.3.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-117"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone calling the API can hide fake log lines inside their request, so the logs investigators rely on can be faked or made unreadable.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Encode request and response bodies before writing them to logs",
        "given": "the gateway logs full request and response bodies to the central log system",
        "when": "a caller submits a body containing newlines, control characters or text shaped like a log record",
        "then": "the body is escaped and stored as a single structured field attributed to the gateway, so it cannot create or alter log records, and it is rendered or exported as inert text"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
